          Miami-Dade Supervisor of Elections Announces Key Dates, Voting Options and Early Voting Locations for November 3 Election

          MIAMI-DADE ( September 01, 2026 )–

          The Miami-Dade County Office of the Supervisor of Elections is reminding voters to prepare now for the 2026 General Election on Tuesday, November 3, with multiple convenient ways to cast a ballot.

          “Every election is an opportunity for your voice to be heard, and we want to make sure every Miami-Dade voter has the information needed to participate,” said Miami-Dade Supervisor of Elections Alina Garcia. “Whether you vote during Early Voting, by mail or on Election Day, we encourage you to make your plan now and make your voice count.”

          Key Election Dates and Deadlines

          • Election Day: Tuesday, November 3, 2026, from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.
          • Voter Registration Deadline: Monday, October 5, 2026
          • Vote-by-Mail Request Deadline: Thursday, October 22, 2026, at 5 p.m.
          • Early Voting: Monday, October 19, through Sunday, November 1, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. daily
          • Vote-by-Mail Ballot Return Deadline: Tuesday, November 3, by 7 p.m.

          Vote-by-Mail ballots may be returned to Elections Headquarters in Doral or Downtown Branch Office by 7 p.m. on Election Day. During Early Voting, voters may also return Vote-by-Mail ballots at any Early Voting location during Early Voting hours.

          Early Voting

          Miami-Dade County will offer 28 Early Voting locations from October 19 through November 1. All locations will be open daily from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.

          Early Voting locations:

          1. Arcola Lakes Branch Library, 8240 NW 7th Avenue, Miami
          2. Miami Dade College Kendall Campus — The Fascell Conference Center, 11011 SW 104th Street, Building K, Miami
          3. Coral Gables Branch Library, 3443 Segovia Street, Coral Gables
          4. Miami Lakes Community Center, 15151 NW 82nd Avenue, Miami Lakes
          5. Coral Reef Branch Library, 9211 SW 152nd Street, Miami
          6. Naranja Branch Library, 14850 SW 280th Street, Homestead
          7. Florida International University — Student Academic Success Center, 11200 SW 8th Street, Miami
          8. North Dade Regional Library, 2455 NW 183rd Street, Miami Gardens
          9. Hispanic Branch Library, 1398 SW 1st Street, Suite 100, Miami
          10. North Miami Public Library, 835 NE 132nd Street, North Miami
          11. Historic Garage, 3250 S Miami Avenue, Miami
          12. North Shore Branch Library, 7501 Collins Avenue, Miami Beach
          13. Homestead Community Center, 1601 N Krome Avenue, Homestead
          14. Northeast Dade-Aventura Branch Library, 2930 Aventura Boulevard, Aventura
          15. International Mall Branch Library, 10315 NW 12th Street, Doral
          16. Office of the Supervisor of Elections, 2700 NW 87th Avenue, Doral
          17. John F. Kennedy Library, 190 W 49th Street, Hialeah
          18. Rebeca Sosa Multipurpose Facility, 1700 SW 62nd Avenue, West Miami
          19. Joseph Caleb Center Community Meeting Room, 5400 NW 22nd Avenue, Building A, Miami
          20. Shenandoah Branch Library, 2111 SW 19th Street, Miami
          21. Kendale Lakes Branch Library, 15205 SW 88th Street, Miami
          22. South Dade Government Center, 10710 SW 211th Street, Lobby, Miami
          23. Kendall Branch Library, 9101 SW 97th Avenue, Miami
          24. Stephen P. Clark Government Center — Elections Branch Office, 111 NW 1st Street, Lobby, Miami
          25. Lemon City Branch Library, 430 NE 61st Street, Miami
          26. West Kendall Regional Library, 10201 Hammocks Boulevard, Miami
          27. Miami Beach City Hall, 1700 Convention Center Drive, Miami Beach
          28. Westchester Regional Library, 9445 SW 24th Street, Miami

          Some Early Voting locations have been temporarily relocated. Voters are encouraged to check the Office of Elections website for the most current location information before heading to the polls.

          A secure ballot intake station will be available at all Early Voting sites for voters to conveniently drop off their Vote-By-Mail ballots.

          Know Before You Go

          Miami-Dade County has 767 precincts and 516 polling locations for the 2026 General Election.

          Voters are encouraged to verify their registration status, polling location and other election information before voting. On Election Day, voters cast their ballots at their assigned precinct only, which is on their voter information card. 

          For complete information about the 2026 General Election, including voter registration, Vote-by-Mail, Early Voting locations and Election Day information, visit www.votemiamidade.gov.

          About the Miami-Dade County Office of the Supervisor of Elections

          The Miami-Dade County Office of the Supervisor of Elections is committed to conducting secure, accurate, transparent and accessible elections and providing Miami-Dade County voters with the information and resources they need to participate in the democratic process.

          # # #

          To request materials in accessible format, sign language interpreters, and/or any accommodation to participate in any County-sponsored program or meeting, please contact the ADA Coordinator, five days in advance to initiate your request. TTY users may also call 711 (Florida Relay Service).

          Alina Garcia, Miami-Dade Supervisor of Elections
